# Failure-aware evidence fusion

::: {.hub-idea-hero}
<p class="hub-idea-status">Idea · High priority · 2/9 readiness fields complete</p>

## What does this mean?

Use a reliability check to choose which evidence sources should influence each request.

## Why does it matter?

Response and reference evidence help unevenly, so a fixed mixture can hide failures.

<figure class="hub-causal-comparison">
<section class="hub-causal-current">
<h3>Today</h3>
<p>One fixed evidence mixture creates uneven failures.</p>
<ul>

</section>
<div class="hub-causal-change" aria-hidden="true"></div>
<section class="hub-causal-proposed">
<h3>Proposed</h3>
<p>A reliability gate chooses the evidence mixture.</p>
<dl>

<dt>Known request pattern</dt>
<dd>Use similar historical requests.</dd>
</div>
<div>
<dt>Stable candidate strength</dt>
<dd>Use semantic profiles.</dd>
</div>
<div>
<dt>Response evidence passes checks</dt>
<dd>Use responses or references.</dd>
</div>
</dl>
</section>
<figcaption class="hub-decision-test">Does the adaptive mixture beat the frozen dense/profile control?</figcaption>

## How does it work?

<ol class="hub-record-path">
<li class="hub-record-path-step">Read the new request and estimate which evidence sources are dependable.</li>
<li class="hub-record-path-step">Choose a bounded evidence mixture using the frozen reliability rule.</li>
<li class="hub-record-path-step">Rank candidates and compare with the frozen dense/profile control.</li>
</ol>
